newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper bows to pressure for reshuffle.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper bows to pressure for reshuffle.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper, in his second cabinet reshuffle in a week, on Friday named two new ministers in a widely expected shakeup that had been demanded by a powerful faction of the ruling Liberal Party.
Samper told reporters the ministries of Agriculture and Environment were the latest in a long line of government offices to see changes at the top since he took office in August 1994.
The move came just one week after Samper appointed new Labour and Foreign Trade ministers.

Samper said Cecilia Lopez, a veteran member of his government team, had been removed as Agriculture minister and appointed head of the National Planning Department instead. To replace her, he named Antonio Gomez Merlano, the director of a government agency responsible for financing public works projects.
Samper also said Eduardo Verano de la Rosa, head of the presidential office for Atlantic Coastal Affairs, had been named to take over from Jose Vicente Mogollon as Environment minister.

Gomez Merlano and Verano are both from the Caribbean coast and their appointments had been demanded by Sen. Jose Guerra Tulena, a veteran leader of the Atlantic or Caribbean coastal provinces in Congress.

Provincial leaders often vote in a bloc and Samper, whose government has been severely weakened by the drug corruption scandal that nearly drove him out of office, could not easily afford to ignore demands from his supporters for larger quotas of bureaucratic power.
"This represents a tribute to the Atlantic coast," Samper said in announcing Friday's appointments.

Guerra Tulena, whose political power base is in northern Sucre province, has been a staunch supporter of Samper's policies in Congress. He was president of the Senate last year when Congress absolved the president of any wrongdoing in connection with charges that he received millions of dollars in drug money to finance his 1994 camapaign.
